judge_assessment.explanation: I recomputed every value the judge listed and all ten agree: 110/2 = 55; 180-84 = 96 and 180-71 = 109; the inscribed 40 deg gives an 80 deg arc, so (80/360)(2*pi*9) = 12.566 -> 12.6 cm; 8x = 72 gives x = 9; (144/360)*pi*100 = 125.66 -> 125.7; 180-90-34 = 56; x^2+y^2-10x-6y+9 = 0 becomes (x-5)^2+(y-3)^2 = 25 with x-intercepts 1 and 9; 12^2 = 8(8+x) gives x = 10; 49*pi - 98 = 55.938 -> 55.9; and x^2+y^2-8x+6y-11 = 0 becomes (x-4)^2+(y+3)^2 = 36 with a 120 deg sector of 12*pi = 37.699 -> 37.7. The ACCEPT verdict is right and no mathematics is wrong. Where I part company is the clarity/print score of 4: the judge did not check the answer LOCATIONS. worksheet.tex problem 7 is \problem[8cm]{...} with parts (a) and (b) and no \answerline, so the preamble auto-emits exactly ONE "Answer: ____" for four verified values (centre 5, centre 3, radius 5, intercepts [1, 9]); problem 10 prints \answerline{m} and \answerline{m$^2$} for three requested values, leaving the centre (4, -3) with no slot even though verify.json verifies both of its coordinates. The preamble's own comment calls this condition "worse than none", so it is a documented defect the judge missed.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 6 carries a declared, machine-checked trap: 180-34 = 146 is the value a student produces after forgetting that an angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle, and the key prints it under Common wrong answers, so the missing theorem is diagnosable from the wrong answer alone.

The diagrams are deliberately value-free - problem 9 states r = 14 cm and the right angle AOB in prose while the figure only shades the segment - which removes nearest-figure misattribution on a six-page sheet where a circle picture sits beside almost every problem.

Problem 10 chains completing the square to a sector area, and verify.json splits it into four separate checks (centre x = 4, centre y = -3, r = 6, area 37.7) instead of one lumped answer, so a student who loses only the sign on the y-shift is still credited with the sector work.

The study guide's four sections each end in a try-it whose answer is itself verified in verify_study_guide.json (e.g. x^2+y^2-8x+2y-8 = 0 -> centre (4, -1), r = 5), so the reference card cannot drift from the worksheet.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author "Answer location (every problem gets one)" and \problem emits exactly one blank per positive workspace, so a problem asking for four values is guided toward a single undifferentiated blank. Nothing in the gate chain relates the number of printed blanks to the number of verified values.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 7 (\problem[8cm]) asks for the centre, the radius and the two x-intercepts and prints one auto-emitted "Answer: ____"; verify.json id 7 holds four entries.
worksheet.tex problem 10 prints \answerline{m} and \answerline{m$^2$}: two blanks for the centre, the radius and the sector area.
answer_key.pdf's Quick Answers prints "7. 5, 3, 5, 1, 9" and "10. 4, -3, 6, 37.7" - unlabelled runs of numbers, which is what one lumped blank forces on the grading column.
templates/worksheet-preamble.tex documents the failure mode itself: "One 'Answer: ____' under a problem whose three sub-parts each need their own answer is worse than none".

improvements.title: One answer blank per requested value - no lumped blank, no orphan blank
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md's "Answer location (every problem gets one)" should read "every REQUESTED VALUE gets one": a multi-part problem ends each part with its own \ansline/\answerline inside the stem (which already suppresses \problem's automatic blank, as the preamble documents), and no problem emits a trailing unlabelled blank once every part already has one. Extend tests/check_answer_line.py, which today only binds units, to compare answer-location macros against the distinct non-manual verify entries for the problem id and fail in both directions. Here problem 7 must print four blanks (centre, radius, and the two intercepts) and problem 10 three, matching their four and three verify entries.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture pair for tests/check_answer_line.py: (a) a problem printing one \ansline against four verify entries must exit non-zero, and (b) the same problem with one \ansline per part must exit 0; plus (c) a problem whose parts all carry blanks and which then emits a trailing \ansline must exit non-zero. All three pass today because the checker never counts blanks.
improvements.expected_impact: The student knows where each requested value goes and the grader can map a Quick Answers row onto the sheet position by position.
improvements.risk: Per-part blanks consume vertical space, so a few dense sheets will gain a page; the gate must also allow a deliberate \noansline on sketch/proof items.

case_summary: A genuinely strong multi-theorem circle review: ten problems, six of which chain two theorems, all seventeen machine checks recomputed correct, one correctly flagged open item (10c), and a study guide whose try-its are themselves verified. The ACCEPT and the mathematics stand. The one real defect is layout-side and systemic rather than mathematical: problems 7 and 10 print fewer answer blanks than the values they demand, so the student has nowhere to commit the centre or the intercepts and the Quick Answers bank degenerates into unlabelled number runs.
